description: The `createNewComment` endpoint at POST `/xxe/simple` calls `comments.parseXml(commentStr, false)`, passing `securityEnabled=false`. Inside `CommentsCache.parseXml`, the `XMLInputFactory` is created without any protective settings when `securityEnabled` is false — specifically, `IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES` and `SUPPORT_DTD` both remain `true` by default (confirmed via runtime test). This allows an attacker to embed a DOCTYPE declaration with an ENTITY that references the filesystem (e.g., `file:///etc/passwd`) or an internal network resource. The resolved content of the external entity is placed into the `Comment.text` field, stored, and returned in the HTTP response — giving the attacker full, unauthenticated local file read capability on the server.

The `getSampleDTDFile` endpoint at `/xxe/sampledtd` is annotated with `@RequestMapping` without specifying an HTTP method, meaning it responds to ALL HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH). CSRF protections are typically only enforced on state-changing verbs when explicitly declared. Any cross-origin request (e.g., via an ``, `
`, or `fetch` from an attacker page) can trigger this endpoint. While this particular endpoint is read-only (returns a DTD template), the broader pattern of unrestricted HTTP methods can bypass CSRF token enforcement in frameworks that only check POST, and may enable CORS pre-flight bypass or cache poisoning on shared proxies.
finding_type: Missing HTTP Method Restriction / CSRF Risk
